name: Brookhaven muon-neutrino discovery experiment (1962)
summary: The 1962 Brookhaven experiment established that the neutrino accompanying a muon is distinct from the electron neutrino, opening accelerator neutrino physics and the study of lepton families.
physics_targets: Distinction between muon and electron neutrinos
detection_principle: A proton beam produced pions whose decays created a neutrino beam. A massive shield absorbed charged particles; neutrinos interacted in aluminium spark chambers. Long penetrating tracks were identified as muons, while electron-like showers were absent at the rate expected for a single neutrino species.
